title: A single-cell atlas of meningioma

publications.title: Spatially resolved single-cell analyses of human meningioma identify novel cell states influencing tumor microenvironment and progression.

institution: University Health Network / University of Toronto
needs_manual_review_reason: NEW RECORD (2026-07-11), from a discovery-log LEAD describing this as '>7.5 million total cells... profiled using single-nuclear RNA sequencing and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics' and flagging it as likely the single highest-value flagship dataset of the search round. Independently verified live via the EGA Metadata API (study EGAS50000001589, dataset EGAD50000002272, samples endpoint). IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the lead: the study-level abstract does describe a combined snRNA-seq + spatial-transcriptomics atlas ('>7.5 million total cells... from meningioma and surrounding dura'), but the actually REGISTERED dataset under this specific accession pair (EGAD50000002272) contains only the single-nucleus RNA-seq arm: num_samples=94, matching 94 distinct registered EGAN sample accessions with subject IDs MNG001-MNG094 (all phenotype 'tumor', 70 female/24 male). The dataset's own description states 'snRNAseq, n=102 samples and 580,185 high-quality nuclei' (102 sequencing libraries from the 94 registered subjects) as well as 'high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (Visium HD, n=43 samples and 7,146,538 segmented cells)', but that spatial arm turns out to be a SEPARATE EGA study/dataset registration: EGAS50000001556 / EGAD50000002233 ('Spatial transcriptomics of human meningioma samples', released the same week, same policy_accession_id EGAP00001001109), whose own 43 registered samples have subject IDs MNG095-MNG137, i.e. a numerically contiguous but entirely DISJOINT patient set from this record's 94 (verified directly, no overlapping subject IDs). Because the two arms use non-overlapping patients, this is NOT a matched multi-modal cohort in the schema's sense (paired_multimodal/multi_modal_matched requires the SAME patients profiled by >=2 modalities); modality here has been corrected to snrna_seq only (not snrna_seq+spatial_transcriptomics as the lead suggested) to reflect what this specific accession pair actually contains, with the spatial arm logged as its own cross-linked record (egas50000001556-spatial-transcriptomics) per instructions not to double-count. Combined, the two arms form one 137-patient 'single-cell atlas of meningioma' flagship project; that combined framing is noted here and on the sibling record but each record's own patient_count/sample_count/modality reflects only its own registered accession. No linked publication (pubmed_ids empty on both study and dataset records); this is a very recently released (2026-04-21) pre-print-less deposition, likely pending its primary publication. The abstract's mention of 'surrounding dura' (implying included normal control tissue) could not be corroborated in the per-sample metadata: all 94 registered samples in this dataset are phenotype 'tumor', with no dura/normal-labeled samples found; normal_control_tissue.included set to false pending resolution, flagged here since a normal-tissue arm may exist but not be separately registered/discoverable yet. Only public EGA study/dataset/sample-level metadata was used per docs/scope.md; the controlled-access sequencing data itself was never accessed. tags.large_cohort left false pending the centralized post-hoc recomputation across the whole inventory noted in docs/schema.md. PUBLICATION LINKED (2026-07-13), prompted by a user question about whether a paper's data-availability statement was fully represented here: Landry et al. 2026 (Nature Genetics, PMID 42265312, DOI 10.1038/s41588-026-02615-w) cites 'EGAD50000002272 for snRNA-seq data' verbatim in its data-availability section (confirmed by fetching the paper's own full-text XML), and its abstract explicitly describes 'a large cohort profiled with single-nuclear RNA sequencing and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics' -- an exact match to this record's own discovery-log description. corresponding_author inferred from Nassiri/Zadeh's last-author position, consistent with this lab's other records in this inventory; no explicit corresponding-author footnote was found in the fetched XML, so kept at Medium confidence. DEEP-AUDIT PASS (2026-07-14): CORRESPONDING AUTHOR CONFIRMED via a direct contrib-group xref check of PMC13263146.xml (Europe PMC fullTextXML, distinct from the earlier fullTextXML fetch that missed the author-notes structure): exactly two contributors carry the corresponding-author (✉) xref -- 'Nassiri Farshad' and 'Zadeh Gelareh' -- matching this record's existing value exactly. Upgraded confidence_level.corresponding_author from Medium to High. AUTHOR LIST CORRECTED: publications[0].authors had been mechanically truncated to the first 6 names; Europe PMC's authorString for PMID 42265312 confirms 18 total authors, now written in full. HIDDEN PER-SAMPLE DATA FOUND IN FULL TEXT: PMC13263146's own 'Study cohort' section states 'Our cohort focused on snRNA-seq (n=102 samples...) and spatial transcriptomics (Visium HD, n=43 samples...). Bulk DNA methylation was used to classify cases by MG using our published model' -- i.e. every case in this exact snRNA-seq accession (EGAD50000002272) is classified by a named Molecular Group (MG) methylation-based subtyping system, not exposed anywhere in the public EGA sample-level metadata. molecular_subtype_annotated corrected from 'Not reported' to true (tags.molecular_subtype_annotated matched); confidence marked Medium since exact per-sample MG counts were not found in the fetched full-text excerpt (likely in a supplementary table not retrieved in this pass). grade_breakdown left null: the paper discusses WHO grade extensively (e.g. 'tissue repair MP was significantly upregulated in WHO grade 1 cases compared to WHO grade 2 or 3 cases') but no exact per-grade sample count specific to this 94-patient/102-sample accession was found in the full text checked; not guessed. has_outcome_data left false/'Not reported': the paper's PFS analysis in the excerpts found ('cycling and metabolic MPs were both associated with shorter progression-free survival') is explicitly described as deconvolved 'from our bulk RNA cohort', a different accession, not this snRNA-seq dataset's own samples, so no outcome-data claim was applied here. brain_invasion checked (2 citation-only hits to an unrelated reference paper on brain invasion criteria, no per-sample data for this cohort) and left unchanged.
